info:
The "passato prossimo," is commonly used to talk about completed actions or events that happened in the past.

It is a compound tense formed by combining a helping verb (either essere or avere) with the past participle of the main verb.

Using "Avere" as the Helping Verb:
For most verbs that take a direct object, "avere" is used.
Io ho mangiato (I have eaten)
Tu hai studiato (You have studied)
Lui/lei ha viaggiato (He/she has traveled)
Noi abbiamo parlato (We have spoken)
Voi avete visto (You have seen)
Loro hanno comprato (They have bought)

Io ho mangiato (I have eaten)
Tu hai studiato (You have studied)
Lui/lei ha viaggiato (He/she has traveled)
Noi abbiamo parlato (We have spoken)
Voi avete visto (You have seen)
Loro hanno comprato (They have bought)
answer: Lei ha nuotato un anno fa
